answer.diagnosis: A 3x3 patch in the top-left corner (image rows 1-3, columns 1-3) is far from the central blob yet carries the largest-magnitude first-layer weights (about ±55 to ±99, versus roughly ±60 for blob weights). The patch is excitatory in units 1, 7, 11, 12, 14, 16 and 19. It is strongly inhibitory in units 3, 5, 8, 17, 20, 23, 25, 30 and 31, and moderately so in unit 10. These are the same units that carry the centre-blob size detectors: the centre-positive disc/ring units and the units that respond to a negative inner ring. So a bright corner marker feeds directly into the size computation. Such a marker cannot reflect blob size, so it is most likely a spurious feature that was correlated with the label in training. Zeroing this corner patch in W1 for all hidden units removes the marker pathway and leaves the centre and ring size detectors intact.
